title: Combined effects of stand density and site quality on stand-level volume growth and ingrowth in Norway spruce selection forests in Norway
content:
Abstract
Using long-term trial data from southeastern and central Norway, spanning up to 100 years of periodic measurements, this study aimed to quantify the combined effects of stand density and site quality on stand-level volume growth and ingrowth in Norway spruce (Picea abies L.) selection forests. Although stand density and site quality strongly influence both studied processes, their joint effects have not previously been examined in Fennoscandia. For this purpose, data from three experimental series with a total of 24 sites representing a broad range of stand densities and site qualities were included in the analysis. Stand density was quantified as both standing volume and basal area. Given the lack of site index systems for selection forests, we applied the locally applicable site index for even-aged stands to quantify site quality. Results show that gross volume increment increases with higher stand density and site quality and could be predicted with similarly high precision using either basal area or standing volume. No evidence of saturation was observed at the upper density levels within the range of the data analyzed, with basal areas and standing volumes well represented up to 40 m2 ha−-1 and 400 m3 ha−1, respectively. While ingrowth averaged 14 trees ha−1 yr−1, its response to stand density appeared to vary with site quality. On the more productive sites, higher stand density was associated with increased ingrowth, whereas on less productive sites, higher density appeared to suppress ingrowth. At medium-quality sites, ingrowth was only marginally affected by density. These findings suggest that recruitment in the studied selection forests may, to some extent, be shaped by the interplay between stand density and site quality. By disentangling these effects with a uniquely large dataset, this study provides new insights into the dynamics and management of Norway spruce selection forests in the boreal Nordic region. Given sufficient stocking, predictions from the derived volume growth models suggest that the disparity in timber production between selection forests and even-aged forests in Norway may be smaller than earlier studies have indicated.
